definition: A molecule that binds a receptor and switches it on — most peptides here are agonists of something.
Reports without controls: forums, testimonials, clinic lore. Our lowest grade, stated plainly.
Bacteriostatic water — 0.9% benzyl alcohol lets a reconstituted vial survive weeks of repeated draws.
Your own pre-protocol values — the median of at least two panels. Drift from this is usually the earliest signal worth having.
The fraction of a dose that reaches circulation. Injection ≈ high; oral peptides usually very low.
Anything measurable that tracks a biological state — ApoB, hs-CRP, IGF-1, resting heart rate.
A planned on/off period for a protocol. The off weeks are part of the design, not a lapse.
Receptors down-regulating under constant stimulation — why pulses beat flat elevation for some pathways.
Growth-hormone-releasing hormone. Sermorelin, CJC-1295 and tesamorelin imitate it.
The hunger hormone — also the receptor GHRPs, ipamorelin and MK-677 use to trigger GH release.
GH-releasing peptide — the ghrelin-receptor family: GHRP-2, GHRP-6, hexarelin, ipamorelin.
Time for blood levels to fall by half. Sets dosing frequency — minutes for sermorelin, a week for GLP-1s.
Hypothalamus–pituitary–testes signalling chain. ‘Keeping the axis alive’ means not letting it go silent.
Insulin-like growth factor 1 — the downstream marker that shows a GH protocol is actually doing something.
Gut hormones (GLP-1, GIP) that regulate insulin and appetite — the pathway behind the weight-loss injectables.
International unit — an activity-based measure. On an insulin syringe, 100 units = 1 mL.
Fat-layer scarring from repeated injections in one spot. The reason site rotation exists.
A short chain of amino acids — smaller than a protein. Most compounds here are 2–50 residues.
Hormones released in bursts rather than steadily. GH secretagogues try to amplify pulses, not flatten them.
Randomized controlled trial — the strongest single study design, and the bar for our top grade.
The cellular lock a peptide’s key fits. Selectivity — hitting one lock only — is what made ipamorelin famous.
Dissolving lyophilized peptide in BAC water at a concentration you chose on purpose.
Subcutaneous — injected into the fat layer under the skin. The default route for most peptides.
Stepping a dose up on a schedule, letting tolerance to side effects catch up before the next step.
The lowest blood level between doses — the consistent moment to draw comparable labs.
The calendar’s per-compound counter: doses left in the current vial and its 28-day use-by date.
